posts.title: The first pour of autumn
posts.excerpt: The furnace was relit last Tuesday after the summer rest. A note on the first pour of the season.
posts.content:
The furnace was relit last Tuesday after the summer rest. A note on the first pour of the season.

Waking the furnace

After six weeks cold, the furnace takes a whole day to dry out before it can be lit properly.

Genzo fires it slowly with charcoal on Monday and listens to it more than he looks at it.

Forty moulds

By Tuesday morning forty moulds were waiting in the sand pit, most of them arare, a few hira for the winter.

The first ladle went into the smallest mould, as it always does: if anything is wrong, it is wrong on a small kettle.

The furnace tells you when it is ready, if you are quiet.

Genzo Ubukata

posts.title: Why we season with tea
posts.excerpt: A used tea bag is the best friend of an iron kettle. Here is why it works, and when to use it.
posts.content:
A used tea bag is the best friend of an iron kettle. Here is why it works, and when to use it.

Tannin and iron

Tea leaves are full of tannin, which joins with iron to make a dark, stable layer on the surface.

That layer is what keeps a kettle from rusting, and it is also why old kettles look so deep and black inside.

When to do it

If you see a little red inside, boil the kettle once with a used tea bag in the water and pour it away.

There is no need to do it on a schedule. The kettle will show you when.

Iron and tea have been friends for a very long time.

Toma Kise

posts.title: Ten thousand hobnails a week
posts.excerpt: Every hobnail on an arare kettle is pressed into its mould by hand. Mio explains how.
posts.content:
Every hobnail on an arare kettle is pressed into its mould by hand. Mio explains how.

The tool

A short rod of hardwood with a rounded tip, worn smooth by three generations of hands.

Mio presses it into the damp clay in rows, turning the mould a little after every one.

A pattern you can feel

The rows are never perfectly even. Run a finger over two arare kettles and you will feel the difference.

Mio keeps a notebook with a rubbing of every pattern, so a kettle can be matched decades later.

The mould forgets nothing your hand does.

Mio Ubukata

posts.title: Water that tastes softer
posts.excerpt: People often say water from an iron kettle tastes rounder. A short note on why that might be.
posts.content:
People often say water from an iron kettle tastes rounder. A short note on why that might be.

What changes

A well-seasoned kettle releases a very small amount of iron into the water, and the baked skin inside seems to take the edge off hard tap water.

We are founders, not chemists, but we have heard the same thing from tea rooms for ninety years.

Try it yourself

Boil the same water in a steel kettle and an iron one, let both cool a little, and taste them side by side.

Most people can tell. Some cannot, and that is fine too.

Good water makes a good cup; the rest is patience.

Toma Kise

posts.title: A morning in the tea room
posts.excerpt: On shop days the small tea room behind the foundry is open to anyone who comes by.
posts.content:
On shop days the small tea room behind the foundry is open to anyone who comes by.

The room

Four tatami mats, a sunken hearth and one hira kettle that is never quite allowed to go cold.

Visitors sit, drink a cup and hold the kettles they are thinking of buying.

Who comes

Tea teachers from the city, people passing through on the way to the hot springs, and our neighbours, who mostly come for the warmth in winter.

A kettle is best chosen with a cup in your hand.

Toma Kise

posts.title: Mending an old kettle
posts.excerpt: Someone sent us their grandmother’s kettle, red inside and silent for twenty years. This is how it came back.
posts.content:
Someone sent us their grandmother’s kettle, red inside and silent for twenty years. This is how it came back.

Taking the rust out

We brushed out the loose rust with a soft brush, then boiled the kettle with tea three times.

The inside turned from red to brown to black, and it stopped colouring the water.

A new lid knob

The knob had cracked, so Genzo cast a new one from the same iron and fitted it the old way, with a copper pin.

It went home sounding just as it should.

An iron kettle is never really broken, only tired.

Genzo Ubukata

products.name: Arare Kettle
products.short: A round kettle covered in hand-set hobnails, the shape the foundry has cast since 1931.
products.description:
A round kettle covered in hand-set hobnails, the shape the foundry has cast since 1931.

Every hobnail on the body is pressed into the clay mould by hand, about 2,400 of them, so no two kettles carry quite the same pattern. The iron holds heat long after the flame is out and softens the taste of the water.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Size: Ø 17 cm · H 21 cm with handle
details.Finish: Baked lacquer outside, bare iron inside

products.name: Natsume Kettle
products.short: A smooth kettle in the shape of a jujube, its walls brushed with a fine comb before casting.
products.description:
A smooth kettle in the shape of a jujube, its walls brushed with a fine comb before casting.

The natsume is narrower at the shoulder than the arare and quicker to boil. Its walls are brushed in the mould with a fine comb, which leaves a soft, almost woven grain on the iron.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Size: Ø 15 cm · H 20 cm with handle
details.Finish: Baked lacquer outside, bare iron inside

products.name: Hira Kettle
products.short: A low, wide kettle that sits close to the fire, with a faint wave pattern around its shoulder.
products.description:
A low, wide kettle that sits close to the fire, with a faint wave pattern around its shoulder.

Hira means flat. The wide base takes heat from a whole brazier at once, so the hira is the kettle for a long afternoon: it holds enough for a table of six and keeps it hot for an hour.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Size: Ø 21 cm · H 17 cm with handle
details.Finish: Baked lacquer outside, bare iron inside

products.name: Kyusu Teapot
products.short: A small iron teapot with a side handle and an enamelled inside, for brewing leaves, not boiling water.
products.description:
A small iron teapot with a side handle and an enamelled inside, for brewing leaves, not boiling water.

The kyusu is lined with a thin coat of enamel fired at 800 °C, so it can hold tea without rusting and is rinsed clean in a moment. A steel mesh basket sits under the lid.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Heat: Not for the flame: for brewing only

products.name: Small Arare Kettle
products.short: The arare in a size for one or two: enough water for a pot of tea, boiled in a few minutes.
products.description:
The arare in a size for one or two: enough water for a pot of tea, boiled in a few minutes.

A squat little kettle with finer hobnails than its larger sister and a handle wrapped in rattan, so it can be lifted without a cloth after a short boil.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Size: Ø 13 cm · H 16 cm with handle
details.Finish: Baked lacquer outside, bare iron inside

products.name: Gotoku Trivet
products.short: A plain iron ring on four short legs that lifts a hot kettle off the table, cast from the same iron.
products.description:
A plain iron ring on four short legs that lifts a hot kettle off the table, cast from the same iron.

Four short legs and a ring, nothing more. The gotoku stands on the table or inside a brazier, and holds any of our kettles steady.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

products.name: Ear Pan
products.short: A small round pan with two short ears, for eggs, a few vegetables or reheating rice.
products.description:
A small round pan with two short ears, for eggs, a few vegetables or reheating rice.

Cast thin for an iron pan, so it warms quickly and is light enough to carry to the table. Season it like a kettle, with a little oil instead of tea.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

products.name: Hand Brazier
products.short: A small round brazier for a few pieces of white charcoal, to keep a kettle warm at the table.
products.description:
A small round brazier for a few pieces of white charcoal, to keep a kettle warm at the table.

Fill it with a bed of ash and three pieces of white charcoal, set a gotoku inside and the kettle on top. It keeps water hot for an afternoon without a sound.

Every piece is cast by hand, so size, weight and texture vary slightly from the photograph. See Seasoning & care before the first boil.

details.Use: White charcoal on an ash bed, outdoors or by an open window
